_comment: Wire hook.py into Claude Code by merging this hooks block into
~/.claude/settings.json (global) or .claude/settings.json (per project).
Replace /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/hook.py with the real absolute path to hook.py
in your clone of this repo.
The SAME hook.py handles every event kind (it dispatches on hook_event_name):
PreToolUse / PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure : before/after snapshot
(matcher limits the tools). PostToolUseFailure fires when a tool FAILS; wiring
it is strongly recommended -- without it, a failed command's partial writes
are not captured. Omit this block if your Claude Code version predates it.
single-file tools: Write / Edit / Read / NotebookEdit / MultiEdit
command tool:      Bash
UserPromptSubmit : record the user's prompt (redacted; no matcher needed)
Stop / SubagentStop : record per-turn token usage from the transcript
UserPromptSubmit / Stop carry no tool_name, so they take no matcher.
Set ALOG_DATA to change the store location (default: <cwd>/.alog).
Set ALOG_DEBUG=1 to print the hook's internal log to stderr.
LARGE-TREE CAUTION: Bash events snapshot the WHOLE work tree, and every new
session's first Bash command pays a cold full-tree read+hash. Wiring this
block globally (~/.claude/settings.json) runs it wherever you start Claude
Code -- in a very large directory the snapshot exceeds the built-in ceilings
(ALOG_MAX_TREE_FILES, default 20000 files; ALOG_MAX_TREE_SECONDS, default 3s)
and is SKIPPED, recorded as a tree_snapshot_skipped event. Prefer per-project
wiring (.claude/settings.json) for big workspaces; set either variable to 0
to disable that ceiling.
EXEC FORM (command + args) is deliberate: the shell form 'python3 /path/to/hook.py'
word-splits on a clone path containing spaces (e.g. /Users/you/AI Tools/agent-trail),
so NONE of the audit hooks would run. With args, the path is passed as one argv
element and never reaches a shell parser.
